1.0.0.en: While the Evangelists Luke and Matthew were concerned with the temporal events of the Nativity, John was concerned to bring out the eternal birth of the Lord Christ, because his first concern was to prove the divinity of Christ in the midst of the doubts the Jews raised against the person of Christ. There is no verse stronger than: "and the Word was God." For this reason, we find that a group such as the Jehovah's Witnesses, who deny Christianity and the divinity of Christ, alter in their book the wording of this verse to: "and the Word was a god." What is meant by the Word is the divine Mind, that is, the Second Hypostasis, because the word expresses the mind, proceeds from it, and is equal to it.

1.0.1.en: The second verse affirms, more clearly, the eternal existence of the Father and the Son. There was no moment, in human language, in which the Father was prior or alone; the eternal birth of the Son is wholly bound up with the existence of the Father, just as we say that the appearing of the disc of the sun is bound up with the going forth of the ray of light from it.

1.1.0.en: A clear indication affirming the divinity of Christ, since He is the Creator, "and without him was not any thing made" of creation (compare Heb 1:2). The Apostle goes on to a spiritual dimension alongside the theological one, and says: "was life," that is, Christ is not only Creator, but the source of the life and strength of all His children who have believed and been baptized (in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit). St. John points to the rejection of Christ by the Jews, which made him describe them as the darkness that did not comprehend the light sent to the world.

1.1.1.en: So, beloved, do you thank the Lord Christ that you are the creature of His hands, whom He made and to whom He gave life, and for whom He wanted fellowship with Him in the light? He who truly believes that he is the center of the Lord's concern finds nothing to offer in return except a life of constant thanksgiving.

1.2.0.en: The talk here is about John the Baptist and his mission, namely, preparing people to receive Christ, and not drawing people to himself and to faith in him.

1.2.1.en: Preparing people to receive Christ is a shared mission of all the people of His Church. The true Christian does not think of himself as a light, but as a reflector of the light of Christ upon all those around him; his witness is either by word, like the witness of John, or by his works and outward conduct, so that all those around him see the light of Christ through him.

1.3.0.en: The talk returns here to the person of Christ the Savior. Although the Lord Christ was the hope of the Jews, and they were waiting for Him, they did not know Him and did not receive Him.

1.3.1.en: This is the condition of Christ today, between those who receive and those who reject, and those who claim to be His children, but by their works do not receive Him, rather they push Him back. For receiving Christ is not a declaration, but the submission of the soul and the will to His will, and the carrying out of His commandments and acting upon them: "Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven" (Mt 5:16).

1.4.0.en: "As many as received him ... even to them that believe on his name": there was, and still is, a special gift for everyone who wants Christ, and it is the gift of sonship to God. Physical birth gives lineage and ancestry, and the earthly inheritance ends in death and passing away. But spiritual birth, whose condition is faith and Baptism (Mk 16:16), gives divine sonship and lineage, and a heavenly inheritance that is sure and does not fade away.

1.4.1.en: We all received this gift freely in the Holy Sacrament of Baptism, which places a great responsibility on the Christian, and a question that keeps presenting itself all the time: is my lineage to the world or to Christ? ... Do I live as one born of the flesh or as one born of the Spirit? Careful attention to this question, and to what we call the daily reckoning of the soul concerning all our deeds, has a great effect on the spiritual life with God.

1.5.0.en: "The Word was made flesh and dwelt among us": a reference to the mystery of the Incarnation, which is one of the basic doctrines of Christianity, that God the Word became flesh. The meaning of "flesh" here is a perfect man, as the Creed indicates, "became incarnate and became man"; that is, Christ the God took a human body, soul and spirit united with His divinity, so that He became perfect God and perfect man (compare 1 Tim 3:16). And "became" does not mean that the divinity was changed into material flesh, or limited by a material body, but means: He united with it.

1.5.1.en: We know that the word "flesh," in the language of the Holy Bible, has one of three meanings:

1.5.2.en: (1) Body: "No man ever yet hated his own flesh" (Eph 5:29).

1.5.3.en: (2) Evil: "and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof" (Rom 13:14).

1.5.4.en: (3) A complete human person: "Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh" (Mt 19:6).

1.5.5.en: The prophet Baruch prophesied of the Incarnation and of dwelling among us when he said: "This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him ... Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men" (Bar 3:36, 38).

1.5.6.en: Besides the dimension of faith in these two verses, we can also draw out the following spiritual meanings: "Was made flesh": the Christian became a son of God, because the only begotten Son of God became man.

1.5.7.en: "Dwelt among us": He lived in our midst as one of us with wonderful humility, experiencing all our pains, feeling for us in all our distress; indeed He is the helper of all who suffer ... for none will feel for you except one who suffered all the suffering for your sake ... this is your Christ (Heb 2:18).

1.5.8.en: "And we beheld his glory, the glory": how hard it is to speak of the glory of God before the Incarnation. When Moses tried to see the glory of God, the answer came to him: "There shall no man see me, and live" (Ex 33:20). But in the Incarnation of Christ, we saw the glory of God incarnate in His miracles, which none can do but God. And as a man, He became, in His example for us, without a single sin, presenting to us the image of the perfect man in whose image we ought to be, without excusing or justifying our sins by the circumstances of the world around us.

1.5.9.en: "As of the only begotten of the Father": this distinguishes the sonship of Christ from our own sonship to God, for the sonship of Christ is a sonship of the divine nature, that is, the begetting of the eternal Word from the Father before all ages. But our sonship, we obtained through faith in the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit through the Holy Sacrament of Baptism.

1.5.10.en: "Full of grace and truth": grace is the free gifts that Christ gives us. And truth is the declaration of the truth of God and faith in Him.

1.6.0.en: This is a witness of John the Baptist, confirming everything he had previously prophesied about the coming of Christ after him, but that He has the first place, and he also points to His eternity.

1.7.0.en: In Christ is all the fullness and satisfaction for those who seek Him among those who believe in His name, and from His fullness John and all Christians received.

1.7.1.en: "Grace for grace": a reference to the difference between the grace of the Old Testament, limited to prophets, promises, hope and commandments, and the grace of the New Testament, in which God spoke through His Son and through His free redemption. The Law gave justification to no one, but was a clarification of the way. But Christ is "the way, the truth, and the life" (ch. 14:6).

1.8.0.en: God wanted to reveal to us the nature of His essence in a way that can be perceived, and there was no way other than the Incarnation of the Word.

1.8.1.en: "In the bosom of the Father": a reference to the union and communion between the Father and the Son. It also means that during the Incarnation of Christ on earth, He did not depart from the Father, but He fills every time and place.

1.8.2.en: "He hath declared him": another affirmation of the eternal unity between the Father and the Son.

1.9.0.en: There were possibilities about the person of John: either he was a false prophet like some before him, or he was Elijah who precedes the Christ (Mal 3:1; 4:5), or a true prophet of whom Moses prophesied (Deut 18:15), or the awaited Christ. For this reason, a delegation of scribes, Pharisees and Levites, representing the order of ministers, was sent to inquire about this powerful figure whose disciples had multiplied. We notice the cunning of the Jews in their question, for they knew that the Christ is from the tribe of Judah and the seed of David, while John was from the tribe of Levi, the tribe of the priesthood. And when John was asked, he did not, in humility, ascribe to himself any of these attributes, but pointed to his mission of preparing the people with the Baptism of repentance to receive Christ, who alone, by His authority, gives the Baptism of the Holy Spirit. He also testified that Christ was standing in their midst and had become incarnate. And in true humility, he ended his speech by saying that he was nothing before the glory of the One coming after him, whose shoe's latchet he was not worthy to unloose, which was among the services of slaves at that time.

1.9.1.en: Perhaps we can draw two lessons from this witness of John:

1.9.2.en: (1) That the mission of every Christian is to bear witness to Christ the God and Savior.

1.9.3.en: (2) That we learn humility, and do not steal God's glory for ourselves, but it is enough of a boast for us to serve His name while prostrate beneath His feet.

1.9.4.en: "Bethabara": it is the place where Joshua crossed with the people into the Promised Land.

1.10.0.en: John reveals to us a new secret from the secrets of the work of the Holy Spirit, for he did not know the person of Christ beforehand, but the work of the Holy Spirit in guidance is what informed John of a clear sign, "like a dove." Through this sign, John became certain that He is the Christ ... Then the Baptist affirms to us, through his witness, that Christ is the Son of God (v. 34), and is the "Lamb of God" given for us as a redemption for the forgiveness of sins (vv. 29, 36), who was at that time coming from the mountain of temptation, to begin His ministry and to offer Himself as a sin offering for the world.

1.10.1.en: John gave his witness in 3 stages: v. 19 to v. 28; v. 29 to v. 34; vv. 35-36 in the hearing of his two disciples, Andrew and John.

1.10.2.en: And now, beloved, what you received in the sacrament of the anointing of the Holy Spirit, the Holy Myron, is able to guide you amid the circumstances and problems of life, so that you live reassured at all times, and even come to know more and more the will of God in your life.

1.11.0.en: The two disciples of John the Baptist heard his witness to Christ and followed Him. Jesus asked them: "What seek ye?" They answered that they wanted to know where He dwelt, so He welcomed them, and they came with Him to His place, and stayed with Him all day; and thus their discipleship to Him began.

1.11.1.en: That God asks you, when you follow Him, what you seek, so that your following may be love for His person with faith and surrender, and not for any ulterior purposes such as personal interest, or show and pride, or merely filling spare time.

1.12.0.en: Andrew was one of the two disciples of John the Baptist who followed Christ, so he called his brother Simon and announced to him the appearing of the Messiah, and took him to Christ, who changed his name to Cephas, that is Peter, which means a rock, a reference to his future ministry in holding fast to the rock of faith and preaching it.

1.12.1.en: It is known in the Holy Bible that some names were changed, heralding the beginning of a great mission, such as Abram who became Abraham, and Jacob who became Israel; and as is customary now in the ordination of bishops, priests and deacons, each of them receives the name of one of the saints to suit his new mission.

1.13.0.en: Jesus headed for the region of Galilee in the north, and continued calling His disciples, where He found Philip, who was from the city of Bethsaida, in which also was the home of Andrew and Peter, and He called him and he followed Him. Philip told his friend Nathanael that they had found the awaited Christ, who is the son of Joseph, who is from the city of Nazareth. It appears from Philip's words that the goal of the Law and the prophecies is the awaited Messiah. This Nathanael is the one whose name later became Bartholomew, and he is one of the disciples of Christ.

1.14.0.en: As for the haste in judgment into which Nathanael fell, and the sweeping condemnation of all the people of Nazareth: we learn from it not to judge anyone, for perhaps, without knowing, we fall into condemning saints, as Nathanael judged Christ Himself.

1.14.1.en: The Jews knew that the Christ comes from Bethlehem, the city of David (Mic 5:2; Mt 2:5, 6; Jn 7:42), and not from Nazareth of Galilee.

1.15.0.en: When Christ saw Nathanael, He greeted him by saying that he was an Israelite, that is, not one of the Gentiles scattered in the region of Galilee. Nathanael marveled and asked Him: "Whence knowest thou me?" Jesus continued His words, that He had known him for a long time, when he was under the fig tree. This is a secret story that no one knew except Nathanael and his mother. When Herod ordered the killing of the children in Bethlehem who were less than two years old, Nathanael's mother was afraid and hid her child under a fig tree, and kept watching him from afar. The soldiers searched the whole region and killed the children, but did not find the place of Nathanael, and left. Then she took him and raised him secretly, away from all eyes, so that he would not be killed. And when he grew up, she told him the story of his escape from death, and he kept it as a secret within himself, until Christ revealed it to him when He met him. So Nathanael became certain that Jesus is the awaited Messiah, who knows the unseen, and he declared that He is the Son of God and the King of Israel.

1.15.1.en: We must not fail to note that the Child Jesus was not in Bethlehem at that time, but on His way to Egypt with His mother St. Mary and Joseph the carpenter.

1.16.0.en: Jesus added to Nathanael that his faith would increase, not because he had seen Christ who knows the unseen, but for greater things he would see in following Him, namely the accomplishment of redemption on the Cross, by which He reconciles the heavenly beings with the earthly, and the angels ascend with the prayers of the believers to heaven through Christ the Redeemer, and descend from heaven with many blessings through Christ also, the Savior of the world.

1.16.1.en: The wedding at Cana of Galilee; the cleansing of the temple

2.0.s.en: (1) The wedding at Cana of Galilee

2.0.0.en: The town of Cana lies in the north of Palestine, near the region of Galilee, and is 15 kilometers east of Nazareth. Despite the weariness of fatigue and travel, the Lord Christ did not hesitate to go and attend out of courtesy. For sharing is one of the forms of love, especially that in which effort is expended, and it was also in honor of marriage, which He would make one of the sacraments of the Church.

2.0.1.en: So three days after the calling of Nathanael, the Virgin Mary was invited, as well as Christ and His disciples, to the wedding feast in the city of Cana.

2.1.0.en: The love and motherhood of the Virgin appear in her sensing the need of those around her without their asking.

2.1.1.en: It seems that the number of those who came to the wedding was much greater than expected, so the prepared wine ran out, which was the juice of grapes, naturally fermented, without distillation or the addition of alcohol, that is, by the action of bacteria only, and if it became old, the taste of vinegar appeared in it, but it does not become like the intoxicating wine sold in the markets now, which the Holy Bible forbids.

2.1.2.en: The Virgin hastened, with love, to ask Christ to rescue the people of the wedding from this embarrassment. It was not in God's plan to begin His miracles and His preaching now, so He said to her: "Woman, what have I to do with thee?" that is, you are a human being, and you do not know the wisdom of God and the time He has appointed. But at the same time He honored her, because she is His mother, the holy Virgin Mary, and He answered her intercession.

2.1.3.en: The faith of the Virgin appears in that Christ accepts her intercession, in her asking the servants to do whatever He commands them.

2.1.4.en: My beloved brother, ask God for everything you need, however difficult it may seem, for He loves you ... and seek the intercession of the saints because of their great standing with Him, especially the Virgin Mary.

2.2.0.en: There were in the house six waterpots, that is, large basins, which they filled with water to wash with in the Jewish purifications according to the Law, and each pot held about 80 liters. Christ told the servants to fill them completely with water, then commanded them to bring it to the ruler of the feast. When he tasted the water that had been turned into wine, he felt that it was of the good kind, so he rebuked the bridegroom for serving the good wine at the end, and the lesser wine at the beginning, and he did not know that the second wine had been changed from water. The servants felt, and indeed all those at the feast afterward, that they were before a great miracle, for it is a miracle of creation, since Christ created grape juice and alcohol that had not existed. This is the first of the miracles of Christ, and the Church counts it as one of the minor Feasts of the Lord, and celebrates it on the third day after the Feast of Theophany.

2.3.0.en: The Lord Christ took Capernaum as a base for His dwelling and for setting out to minister after Nazareth, and it was an important city lying on the Sea of Galilee in the north.

2.3.1.en: "His brethren": the Church believes in her doctrine and tradition that the holy Virgin Mary did not bear in the flesh anyone but the person of the Lord Jesus, keeping her virginity, and never knew her betrothed Joseph physically at all, which confirms that Christ, in the flesh, had no brothers from Mary. This is what Ezekiel said in his prophecy: "then he shall go forth; and after his going forth one shall shut the gate" (Ezek 46:12). As for His brethren, they are cousins, since the tradition in the Levant, even to this day, is that cousins are called brothers.

2.4.0.en: The Passover of the Jews was the most important of their religious feasts. They would come from all over the world to Jerusalem, where the temple of Solomon was, to offer sacrifices and celebrate this great feast. And this is what the Lord Jesus Himself did. And upon His entering the temple, John reveals to us what the Lord saw and what grieved His heart, indeed angered Him, namely that the porches of the temple had been turned into something resembling a marketplace, for there were the tables and the animals and every kind of trade, and the shouting and all the clamor that occurs in markets, which is contrary to the dignity of the house of God and the loss of the purpose of worship. The text here is explicit, and shows the decisiveness of the Lord Christ, and His zeal for His house and the house of His Father, in what He did. There is a difference between feverish, sinful anger, which many justify for themselves and which God condemns, and righteous zeal and holy anger over my sins, or to rescue the oppressed, or for the sake of the house of God and its rights. My beloved brother, how much we also need now to have the same zeal for the Church, which is the house of God and of the angels and the saints. And God is very jealous for His glory and His house ... and perhaps we too, the children of the Church, cause others to stumble by our conduct and our appearance, which do not befit the dignity of the house of God, the heaven on earth, of which David says: "Holiness becometh thine house, O Lord, for ever" (Ps 93:5).

2.4.1.en: A very frightening question that we ask ourselves: what if the Lord came now and visited His Church, as He visited His temple?!! Would everything He sees please Him? ... Begin with yourself.

2.5.0.en: However, the Jews, the priests and the merchants did not accept what the Lord had done. For this reason they asked Him: "What sign shewest thou unto us" ... as Moses did to Pharaoh to prove that God had sent him? Its meaning is: by what authority do you do this, for you are not one of the ministers or priests, and you are not a worker of wonders or miracles, that we should listen to you.

2.5.1.en: This is what is contrary, in our life, to submission to the commandments and works of God. For one of the most important conditions of faith, as we have pointed out, is believing without demands or material confirmations.

2.5.2.en: We note that the Lord Christ, during the period of His ministry, attended the Passover 4 times: this is the first of them. The second (ch. 5:1), where He healed the sick man of Bethesda. The third (ch. 6:4), where He fed the multitudes. And the fourth (ch. 11:55), where He was crucified.

2.5.3.en: The Lord cleansed the temple twice: this time at the beginning of His ministry, and the second time at the end of His ministry on earth, four days before the Crucifixion (Mt 21:12, 13; Mk 11:15-17; Lk 19:45, 46).

2.6.0.en: When the Jews asked for a sign, the Lord Christ surprised them with what they did not expect, that they would destroy the temple and He would raise it up in three days. And because what He said was a prophecy about His death and Resurrection, they did not understand, but scoffed mockingly!! As for the forty and six years, the time of the building of the temple, it has another story ... The temple was first built on the same site, and Solomon built it in 950 B.C. in 7 years, and the Babylonians destroyed it. Then Zerubbabel built it in 515 B.C. Then Herod restored it, beginning in 16 B.C. until 30 A.D., the time of the preaching of Christ, and this is the period meant by the 46 years.

2.6.1.en: Perhaps the reader will connect what the Lord said here with what is mentioned in (Mt 12:39; Lk 11:

2.6.2.en: 29), when the Jews asked the Lord for a sign (a miracle), and He answered them also that no sign would be given to them but the sign of the prophet Jonah, foretelling also His death and Resurrection after three days ... and of course the saying was hard and not understood by the Jews ... but such are the prophecies, for they are often hard, and when they come to pass, their truth and the truth of their speaker are proved; and this is what the text confirms, that the disciples understood, and their faith was established after the Resurrection of the Lord from the dead.

2.7.0.en: Despite the faith of many as a result of the miracles the Lord performed, whose number we do not know (compare ch. 21:25), Christ did not commit Himself unto them. This means that He knew what was in the hearts of those around Him ... for He knows that this is not a steadfast faith, but a faith led by amazement, and it is a temporary, shallow faith that does not last. And the expression "for he knew what was in man" is a strong indication of His divinity, which He also confirmed in His ability to raise His body after death.

2.7.1.en: So I wonder, beloved, which kind of faith do we have of those mentioned in (Mt 3:23; Mk 4:2-20)? Is it a firm faith working in our hearts by the Holy Spirit, or is it a theoretical faith that appears in times of ease and disappears at the Cross?

2.7.2.en: The Church teaches us not to rejoice and be deceived by abundant and quick fruit, lest it be a faith resembling the faith of the Jews, who quickly turned around crying out: "Crucify him ... crucify him" ... Amen, O Lord, establish us in Your upright faith. Baptism, faith in Christ
